title: Massive upper GI bleed
stem: Resus 2. Mr Chow, 55, with alcohol-related cirrhosis, has vomited about a litre of fresh blood. He is confused. HR 128, BP 82/50, RR 24, SpO2 95%, GCS 14. Manage him.

phases.title: Resuscitate
phases.goal: Monitoring, access and bloods, the major haemorrhage protocol, and his airway.

phases.title: Drugs and blood
phases.goal: Terlipressin and antibiotics from the cart now; restrictive transfusion when the blood arrives.

phases.title: Risk and endoscopy
phases.goal: Score him, then who scopes him, and what if it cannot be controlled?

events.say: He vomits again: another 500 mL of fresh blood. BP 70/40.
events.untreated: He kept bleeding and terlipressin was never given.

notes:
Checked against NICE CG141 (Acute upper GI bleeding, 2012, updated 2016), the BSG/UK variceal bleeding guideline (2015; BSG 2023 decompensated cirrhosis), Baveno VII (2022), and the HALT-IT trial (2020).

Resuscitate: two large-bore cannulae, bloods (FBC, U&E, LFT, clotting, crossmatch), major haemorrhage protocol if needed, restrictive transfusion (Hb threshold 70–80 g/L, target 70–90; higher in cardiovascular disease) — over-transfusion raises portal pressure. Protect the airway (intubate before endoscopy if confused or vomiting heavily). Risk scores: Glasgow–Blatchford before endoscopy (0 can be discharged); Rockall after.

Suspected variceal bleed: terlipressin 2 mg IV every 4 hours (1 mg if under 50 kg or once bleeding controlled) and prophylactic antibiotics (e.g. ceftriaxone 1 g daily) at presentation; endoscopy within 12 hours of resuscitation (band ligation for oesophageal varices, cyanoacrylate for gastric); balloon tamponade (Sengstaken–Blakemore/Minnesota) as a bridge for uncontrolled bleeding; TIPS for refractory bleeding. Non-variceal: PPI after endoscopy (not before, per NICE), endoscopy within 24 hours. Do not give tranexamic acid (HALT-IT: no benefit, more VTE). Correct coagulopathy only if actively bleeding with specific deficits; lactulose for encephalopathy.

Your notes list 'massive GIB' and 'UGIB + VF' as topics without detail.
